correctness.rationale: Exact bit-vector semantics along permutation atom cycles gives the forbidden (d+1)-window characterization. The order-d de Bruijn graph is bijective with permitted periodic words. Cyclewise independence gives the trace product. Every forbidden window has probability at least 2^{-k(d+1)} when realizable; disjoint windows prove uniform exponential decay for long cycles and a finite, attained sharp-gap optimization. Fixed subsets of even negation iterates are enumerated by gcd and the sharp valuation minimum is achieved by a prime-power cycle. The accompanying code directly checks subset semantics independently of transfer traces (10 equation templates, 11588 assignments on cycles), 918 small permutational models, and even exponents through 80; only the proof covers all finite sizes.

value.rationale: Addresses a motivated universal family of quantitative algebraic-logic questions: all term equations on finite Boolean-type Ockham algebras with bijective dual negation. A single finite algebra decides universal validity, a finite exact algorithm computes and attains the strongest probability gap, and the iterate family yields an explicit arithmetic invariant depending on prime valuations. This gives more than routine substitution or a finite census while honestly restricting the algebraic signature and semantics.
